conventions.convention: Forward maps have nonempty open domains in real Hilbert spaces; linear maps are allowed. Derivatives are bounded real-linear Fréchet derivatives.
An x₀-minimum-norm solution minimizes distance to x₀ globally over exact solutions on U. The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness, and x₀ need not belong to U.

The local TCC fixes a single basepoint x and its derivative F′(x), uses every increment of norm at most δ, requires the entire closed ball to lie in U, and requires 0 ≤ η < 1. It does not assert a uniform two-point condition.
The uniqueness theorem assumes x†−x₀ ∈ ker(F′(x†))⊥ and concludes local minimum-norm uniqueness, allowing other exact solutions at strictly greater distance from x₀.

load_bearing.statement: For real Hilbert spaces X,Y, an open U, F:U→Y Fréchet differentiable at x, δ>0 with the closed δ-ball about x contained in U, and 0≤η<1, the local TCC is ‖F(x+h)−F(x)−F′(x)h‖ ≤ η‖F(x+h)−F(x)‖ for every ‖h‖≤δ.
Under the stated local TCC at x, for every h with ‖h‖≤δ, (1−η)‖F(x+h)−F(x)‖ ≤ ‖F′(x)h‖ ≤ (1+η)‖F(x+h)−F(x)‖.
Let X and Y be real Hilbert spaces and U⊆X a nonempty open set. A nonlinear forward model is a map F:U→Y, with no linearity assumed and linear maps allowed; S_F(y)={x∈U:F(x)=y}.
For the stated real-Hilbert open-domain forward map F, y∈Y and x₀∈X, x†∈U is an x₀-minimum-norm solution if F(x†)=y and ‖x†−x₀‖≤‖x−x₀‖ for every x∈U with F(x)=y.

Triangle inequality, homogeneity, nonnegativity and separation in the residual comparison and uniqueness proofs.
Identification of increments annihilated by F′(x†) as kernel vectors.
Squared-distance decomposition for the two orthogonal vectors x†−x₀ and x−x†.
The one-coordinate Euclidean inner product st used to identify the real line as an inner-product space.
The usual absolute-value norm on the one-coordinate Euclidean space.
Completeness of the real line in the examples.
Real inner-product axioms and induced norm for the scalar examples.
